question.text: Ganga Resolution Fund (Cat I SSF) wants to bid as a Resolution Applicant in the CIRP of 'Yamuna Steel'. Under Chapter 9's SSF definition, what SPECIAL privilege does an SSF have?

answer.text: SSF has no special IBC privileges.
SSF can act as a Resolution Applicant under the IBC, 2016, in accordance with its investment objectives — a privilege specifically recognised in the Chapter 9 SSF definition.
SSF can only participate in liquidation, never in resolution.
SSF must mandatorily exit before IBC admission of any investee.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Special Situation Fund means a Category I AIF that invests in special situation assets in accordance with its investment objectives and may act as a resolution applicant under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), 2016.' This is a recognised regulatory accommodation enabling SSF to bid as RA. The Trap: Options A, C, D strip the specific RA privilege. This is the differentiator between SSF and general Cat II stressed-debt funds. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C covers IBC framework in detail. XIX-A covers SSF at distributor level. Manager's Pro-Tip: When bidding as RA, align the SSF's investment policy statement to include 'resolution applicant' explicitly. Also, keep the Resolution Plan financials audit-ready — CoC scrutiny and NCLT scrutiny are both intense.
